note: Parity cases for the deadline due-date phrasing, shared by two suites. tests/unit/chronos-dates.test.ts checks the migrated SvelteKit surface against them; tests/unit/test_chronos_parity.py keeps the `legacy` column honest against the rule the retired NiceGUI service applied, which it now carries itself because issue #102 deleted the page that did. Both have to agree, which is what makes this a parity fixture rather than two independent expectations. Offsets are plain seconds, so every case is timezone- and DST-independent by construction. `now` is half an hour before Europe/Vienna springs forward, and the last two cases are the ones that discriminate: an implementation that compared calendar dates instead of flooring elapsed seconds would get both of them wrong, and only those two.

cases.why: three and a half days out
a day and a half out
half a day past, which floors to a whole day overdue
a day and a half past
23.5 hours across the Europe/Vienna spring-forward boundary: still today, though the local calendar date has already changed
20 minutes past, on the same local calendar day: already a whole day overdue, because the count floors elapsed seconds rather than comparing dates
